cohort: The study cohort consisted of 2920 women of various age groups attending urology and gynecology outpatient departments in a tribal area of Rajasthan, India.
finding: The prevalence of urinary incontinence was 19.93%, with urge incontinence being the most common type, and several factors including age, BMI, parity, mode of delivery, post hysterectomy, chronic cough, diabetes, constipation, and depression were significantly associated with incontinence.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was identified as a significant risk factor associated with urinary incontinence.
